blocks.content: The Governor of a State shall, as soon as may be within one year from the commencement of the Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act, 1992, and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year, constitute a Finance Commission to review the financial position of the Panchayats.

rows: Tax distribution between Union and States
Tax distribution between State and Local Bodies (PRIs/ULBs)

items: Article 243I pertains to Panchayats, while Article 243Y extends the same provisions to Municipalities.
The Central Finance Commission (Article 280) suggests measures to augment the State Consolidated Fund based on recommendations made by the State Finance Commission.
The report of the State Finance Commission is submitted to the Governor, NOT the Chief Minister or State Legislature directly.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The State Finance Commission (SFC) is a constitutional body established under Article 243I (for Panchayats) and Article 243Y (for Municipalities).
The Governor of a State constitutes the Commission every five years to review the financial position of local bodies.
Recommends the distribution of net proceeds of taxes, duties, tolls, and fees levied by the State between the State and local bodies.
Suggests principles for determining grants-in-aid to Panchayats and Municipalities from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
The State Legislature determines the composition of the commission, required qualifications of members, and the manner of selection.
The Governor places the recommendations of the SFC along with an Action Taken Report (ATR) before the State Legislature.
